title: Enterprise SDK & client library intake: prioritization framework for language support, auth patterns, and streaming ergonomics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two quarters we've seen a consistent set of enterprise asks for richer SDKs: first-class Node and Python streaming ergonomics, standardized auth patterns that fit both cloud-hosted and private deployments (SSO/SAML + KMS-backed service tokens), and requests for additional language bindings (Go, Java, and Rust) from platform teams. Goal: define a repeatable intake and prioritization approach for SDK/client library requests coming from enterprise customers (sales, CSMs, and dev advocates), scope an initial implementation plan for the highest-value items, and produce a small set of PRDs/tech designs for engineering to estimate.

Scope: This ticket covers non-bug feature triage only: language support roadmap, auth pattern reference implementations and docs, streaming ergonomics improvements (client reconnect/backpressure, chunked messages, resumable streams), and enterprise integration concerns (private deployment auth flows, audit logging hooks, IAM mapping). Excludes runtime server-side changes beyond required API parity.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake rubric defined and published to Confluence for incoming SDK requests (scoring by customer size, security needs, usage patterns, and maintenance cost).
- Prioritized list of SDK work across languages (top-3 to implement in next quarter) with clear rationale.
- Security and compliance constraints documented for enterprise auth patterns; decision on whether a new auth abstraction layer is needed.
- Streaming ergonomics prototype (Node + Python) demonstrating reconnect and resume semantics and a docs sample for customers.
- Linked PRDs/tech designs and a small pilot implementation plan with milestone-driven timeline.
comments: 2026-02-22 - Maya P.: Kicked off intake call with Sales and CSMs. Collected 12 distinct customer asks; recurring themes: better token refresh docs, streaming reconnect, SAML service account patterns for private deployments.

2026-02-25 - Liam O'C.: Drafted initial rubric. Proposed weighted scoring: security (25%), customer revenue potential (20%), integration effort (15%), usage fit (20%), maintenance cost (20%). Shared with Eng leads for feedback.

2026-03-01 - Priya Menon (Eng): Reviewed rubric. Suggest splitting 'security' into 'compliance required' and 'auth surface complexity'. Also flagged that Go/Java bindings have narrower API surface (embeddings + chat) vs full streaming.

2026-03-03 - Maya P.: Ran quick survey with 26 customers (sales-sourced). Results: 46% asked for Node streaming ergonomics; 30% asked for enterprise auth templates (SAML + KMS); 18% asked for Go SDK; 6% for Rust.

2026-03-05 - Design review notes: DES-211 created to capture minimal streaming UX patterns (onmessage vs ondelta events, chunk aggregation). Design suggests API surface options: callback-based, async iterator, and Observable. Prefers async iterator for Node and Python-first.

2026-03-07 - Security review (initial): security-req-114 opened. Security recommends a recommended pattern for long-lived service tokens that are rotated via KMS + short-lived session tokens for SDKs in shared environments. Also requires threat model doc before rollout.

2026-03-09 - Decision: prioritize Node streaming ergonomics + Python auth-pattern docs as phase 1 (highest customer demand and lowest infra risk). Go SDK scoped for phase 2 as it requires language-specific GC/async modeling.

2026-03-10 - Engineering notes: ENG-3842 (streaming-prototype-node) and ENG-3843 (streaming-prototype-python) spun up. Initial Node prototype demonstrates resumption using stream IDs and token checkpointing. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-prototypes/pull/128
2026-03-11 - PM follow-up: shared PRD link and timeline with Sales to set expectations. Action: CSMs will nominate 2 pilot customers for the Node streaming beta by 2026-03-25.
2026-03-12 - Liam O'C.: Updated priority list and published Confluence doc. Requesting engineering estimates against the PRDs for the planning meeting on 2026-03-15.
notes: If phase 1 pilot goes well, scope for next cycle includes Go SDK baseline (embeddings + chat), additional language idiomatic patterns, and CI/test harness for streaming to reduce maintenance cost. Consider establishing an SDK working group (Eng, DX, Design, Sec) to standardize cross-language primitives and avoid divergence.
